summary.title: Database Internals
summary.one_liner: A book that explains how databases work internally, covering storage engines (B-Trees, LSM-based designs) and distributed systems (failure detection, consistency models, consensus).
takeaways: Databases can be understood as two main parts: storage engines and distributed systems.
Storage engine topics include B-Tree variants, on-disk structures, write-ahead logs, compression, and log-structured storage such as LSM-based designs.
Distributed systems topics include unreliable communication, failure detection, leader election, gossip, and consistency models.
The book references 100+ papers, 10+ books, and several open source database implementations for further study.
summary.summary: This is the online companion page for the book Database Internals, aimed at readers new to databases or interested in developing them. The book is split into two parts: Storage Engines, which covers taxonomy, B-Tree variants, binary formats, page buffers, write-ahead logs, compression, and log-structured storage approaches; and Distributed Systems, which covers process and link models, communication guarantees, failure detection, leader election, gossip, consistency models, atomic commitment and broadcast, and consensus algorithms. The page describes the structure and scope but does not show code or detailed content.
